project.description:
Restores the PIC-SURE dictionary (schema dict) into the picsure database with pg_restore --clean from a pg_dump --format=d tar.
Source: source_dictionary_db_s3_url in build-spec.json of the release-control checkout. It must be s3://<bucket>/<key> with a key ending in .tar (surrounding whitespace is ignored). Anything else is refused ("REFUSED: ...", exit 1) before any AWS call. - In-boundary dump: s3://bdc-etl-data-d0d6191/data/dictionary/db-dumps/dictionary_db_<ts>.tar, written by the pheno job PIC-SURE Dictionary ETL Pipeline/dict-ingest (export-db step). Read as arn:aws:iam::515157839325:role/curated-datasets-s3-role through a temporary AWS CLI profile (credential_source = Ec2InstanceMetadata, selected with --profile), the same way HPDS Data - Stage to Stack Bucket reads a dataset prefix. This role is fixed: it does not follow the global curated_datasets_s3_role. - Legacy dump (any other bucket): read with curated_datasets_s3_role (assume_role before the download, reset_role after it, role skipped when the variable is not set). This is the rollback: put the old legacy URL back in build-spec.json. The log says which source and identity were used.
Before the database is touched the dump is checked: the download is non-empty, it extracts, dump_files/toc.dat exists after the files are flattened into dump_files/, pg_restore --list reads the table of contents, and every TABLE DATA entry has its data file. If a check fails the build fails before the secret fetch, the connection test and pg_restore. Then the secret is fetched through the Bash_Functions job scripts, the connection is tested and pg_restore runs (flags unchanged).
IAM needed for the in-boundary path: curated-datasets-s3-role (515157839325) needs s3:GetObject on bdc-etl-data-d0d6191/data/dictionary/db-dumps/* and s3:ListBucket on that bucket for the prefix data/dictionary/db-dumps/*; its trust policy allows this Jenkins' instance role, which needs sts:AssumeRole on it.
No weights job is needed afterwards: the search weights (concept_node.searchable_fields) are in the dictionary database the dump was taken from, built by the dictionary ETL's reset-weights step (rebuild_searchable_fields.sql, the same tiers as the weights job's defaults), so the restore brings them along.
